d:
Steel yourself for your time in the ruins, young one... You will not be granted free passage there.
Scores of cursed Highborne, now known as naga, roam the once great city. Travel northeast and dispatch them from this land.
What they once were... Is no more. If they aid the Twilight's Hammer, they can bring only further pain to the forests that once gave them shelter.
War is what they seek, adventurer. War... Is what we will bring.
c:
Do not fret, young one. To pillage one's own home for some dark master...
It is unforgivable.

d:
If you'd like to get started doing some good in our world, I'd recommend reporting to a man named Gryan Stoutmantle in Westfall to the south, at the settlement known as Sentinel Hill. His people are in need of aid.
After journeying here from another plane of existence, the problems our lands face may seem small. I assure you, the aid you provide to those impacted by such problems means everything to them, and you will grow stronger for your labors.
Good luck out there, adventurer!
c:
I've been begging Stormwind for aid for months and he sends me a skinny elf? Well, beggars can't be choosers I suppose.
Welcome to Westfall, adventurer. Let's see if we can't put you to work.

d:
After journeying here from the elemental plane, the problems our lands face may seem small. Rest assured, the dangers the horde faces are very real, and you will grow formidable should you survive your service.
If you'd like to get started doing some good in our world, travel southwest to the vast lands known as the Barrens. There is a settlement there known as the Crossroads. The proud citizens there are ever in need of aid.
Go with honor, adventurer!
c:
What's this? An elf? And you say the Warchief sent you?
You look a little skinny to me, but it matters not. Out here you'll either thrive and survive, or you'll die. That is the way of things in these lands.

d:
Attention!
A reward is being offered for the death of the owl "Jai'vhanel" also known as "Swordfeather".
Unfortunately this owl has gone mad and has begun to attack travelers as they journey along the road near Auberdine.
Jai'vhanel was last seen north of the Ameth'Aran ruins near the mountain base. Bring back one of her jet black feathers as proof of her death.
Reward claims for this bounty should be claimed with Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea in Auberdine.
The Auberdine Village Council
p: Greetings, adventurer - what may the Sentinels assist you with today? Perhaps you are here to inquire about the bounty on Jai'vhanel?
c:
It is good to know that issue has been taken care of, but it saddens me that we could not find another way. Jai'vhanel had been somewhat of a guardian of this area for quite some time, and I am not sure what could have caused her descent into madness.
Regardless, thank you for your service today, adventurer. The roads to Auberdine are safe for travel once again.

d:
As you tear away the single page from the Twilight Tome, a foreboding voice floods your mind, uninvited.
They have failed.
You will be forgotten.
They will lose the eye they gained.
p: You look troubled. I am listening.
c:
This bears the mark of an ancient evil, adventurer. I will see it brought to Darnassus at once for further study.
Ande'thoras-ethil.

d:
You're still here?
Take the phial and get out of my sight, druid. It is clear my answers do not lie in the waters, just as they did not before.
Perhaps one of the priestesses in the Temple of the Moon to the south will dispose of it.
I must look elsewhere if this is to work...
c:
Do not mind the Arch Druid, friend. He bears the weight of much in Malfurion's absence.
Wait! Some drops yet remain in the phial! Perhaps that is why his incantation failed?

d:
You must bring this to Tyrande at once! I will transfer it to a more ceremonial container for you.
Do not be afraid. The High Priestess of Elune is firm, but kind. She protects all who enter Darnassus, and carries our goddess' light to all.
She will be glad to receive this sacred water. You will find her directly above us.
p: Please state your business. I have a city to run, and a people to lead.
c:
Staghelm has done much in my beloved's absence, but he is not Malfurion. And he does not run the affairs of Darnassus--that burden is mine alone.
I apologize. As you have likely seen, we have many challenges to overcome.
Fandral is Arch Druid for now, and I ask you respect his station. But his doings pertain to druidism, and mine not only to Elune but indeed to lead our people as she wills.
Every drop of this water is blessed by our goddess. I thank you for saving it.

d:
General Feathermoon ensures all sentinels have time to pray to Elune. A proper huntress wields not blade alone, but gifts of the goddess to overcome our enemies.
You may help with my daily duties. Place sentinels around the city--start with the tunnels leading beneath Cenarion Hold to the north, the bank at the center of town, the inn in the Craftsman's Terrace to the northeast, and the city gates. The guards can assist you.
Something is amiss in Teldrassil--we must remain vigilant.
c: I thank you for your aid. Though I find peace in the daily rituals, it is nice to have a moment to reflect instead.

d:
Those wretched harpies! They attacked the last caravan I had scheduled to deliver supplies to Freewind Post. We have enough supplies for the moment, but without more supplies, we'll run short soon.
I'm not sure what the harpies plan to do with the extra supplies, but I would be grateful if you would recover them for me. They make their lair west of here. They can be found both at the base of the cliffside and inside a cave at the top.
p: Have you been able to recover the supplies the harpies stole?
c: Thank you, friend. These supplies will help get us through until the next shipment arrives.

d:
The Screeching Canyon is home to a local band of harpies known for their ferocious nature and raiding tactics. They have ambushed the last few supply caravans that have been brave enough to traverse this place.
I fear if something isn't done soon, there will be no caravans that will dare make the trek to Freewind Post.
Go, slay as many of these harpies as you are able. Return to me once the deed has been done, and I will reward you well for your efforts.
c: This is wonderful news! I will send word to our suppliers that the harpies have been dealt with. At least that is one less threat the future caravans will need to worry about.

d:
Worked a bit o' a trade with the Dun Garok brew-kin. We're not the only ones missin' the vineyards of the Fallrook family, it seems! Most o' the best bottled years are long since drank, but we do have cases of the wine still in the cellars.
Bring this case of Fallrook Varietal to Dun Garok in the southeast and leave it with 'em by their gatherin' fireplace at the bottom of their fort.
In return, carry a sack o' the Homebrew Hops back with ye.
That keep is the closest thing to home around here!

p: Ah, friend! Do you have those scales?
c:
You're a real natural talent! Say, if you ever decide to take a break from the adventuring life, you come on back to your buddy James. I'll put you right to work!
Although, I suppose you'll be even older by then. Oh well!

d:
Now that we can trust you to deliver critical information to our forward spies, there's an extra task for you.
Bring this to Deathstalker Masoj almost directly south of us. He'll have more for you to do once you get there and hand this to him. He is posted on elevated terrain north of the rotten vineyard they call Nethander Stead.
Our plan to take control of these lands continues steadily.
c:
Quaint. A fresh face for the field work.
Well, let's see what you have then.

d:
Our high command inserts strategic troops using bat riders. Key points around the foothills have lost their signaling beacons.
Take these vials. Uncork them in three locations: the hills bordering Dun Garok, the plateau overlooking Dunholde Keep, and the last on the ridge of the Headland above the town of Hillsbrad. The vapors that emanate will be like a potent tuning rod to the senses of the bat, drawing them to the desired drop-off points once more.
Look for crushed empty vials and renew our marks.
c:
Good work. We advance the plans.
Deathstalkers dare.
Let purpose guide your strikes, friend.
